results.title: The $500 Billion Buys the Factories. Utilization Decides the Winners.
results.author: Vishnu Subramanian
highlights:
# The $500 Billion Buys the Factories. Utilization Decides the Winners.

Vishnu Subramanian

Founder @ Jarvislabs

August 11, 2026· 10 min read

On August 10, Nvidia announced partnerships with Apollo, BlackRock, Blackstone, Brookfield, Goldman Sachs and KKR: financing platforms designed to mobilize over $500 billion of third-party capital for AI infrastructure. Jensen Huang's framing was direct: AI factories can now be financed as productive infrastructure, backed by long-term institutional capital. In his words, "in AI, compute is revenue."

...

Here's what that looks like from the ground.

Launch a GPU on Jarvislabs — from $0.41/hr

H100s, H200s, A100s and more — per-second billing, no commitments.

...

Nvidia ships a new GPU generation every two to three years, and the standing question was whether the older generation would become obsolete before it paid for itself.

Two years back, the market behaved exactly that way. A huge wave of supply came in, and providers competed by cutting prices on H100s and H200s. It looked like a race to the bottom.

Over the last year, we've watched that trend reverse. Prices are increasing. Availability has gone down. And customers who used to rent by the hour now want to commit for much longer durations, to make sure the compute they need for their workloads is actually there.

The numbers on our own platform tell the story. When I wrote this in August, our on-demand price was $2.69 per hour for an H100 and $3.99 for an H200, already 20 to 30% higher than a year earlier. As of October 5, it is $3.49 for an H100 and $4.59 for an H200, another 30% and 15% on top of that. For committed capacity, pricing depends on cluster size and duration: a large H200 cluster runs anywhere between $3.20 and $4.00 per hour, and a two- or three-year contract can bring that toward the lower end of $3 to $4.

Here's the detail that surprises people: when customers want an instant cluster, capacity right now rather than next quarter, they usually end up paying more than the on-demand price. Scarcity has inverted the old discount logic.

Nvidia cited the same trend in its announcement: one-year H100 rentals rose from about $1.70 to $2.35 per GPU-hour between October 2025 and March 2026, and cross-provider on-demand medians moved from roughly $2.00 to $2.70. We saw the same movement in our own pricing well before the announcement. The asset is holding value.

results.title: We spent 20 working days getting one model into production. So we built Managed Endpoints.
results.author: Vishnu Subramanian
highlights:
# We spent 20 working days getting one model into production. So we built Managed Endpoints.

Vishnu Subramanian

Founder @ Jarvislabs

August 26, 2026· 8 min read

Over the last several months, we have worked with a number of enterprises that wanted to try open models. Not a chatbot demo. Real work: coding agents, internal tools, pipelines that run all day.

...

So we asked a simple question: since we're doing this work anyway, can we do it once per model and let the customer skip it? That's Managed Endpoints. Pick a model from the catalog, click deploy, get a URL. The catalog currently includes DeepSeek V4 Flash, Gemma 4 31B, GLM-5.2, GLM-5.3 and GLM-5.3 Flash. You can configure how it scales, or take the defaults.

Launch a GPU on Jarvislabs — from $0.41/hr

H100s, H200s, A100s and more — per-second billing, no commitments.

...

## What it costs

You pay per GPU-second of worker runtime. If GLM 5.2 needs an 8×H200 node and it runs for 30 minutes, you're billed for 30 minutes. Our H200 is $4.59 per GPU-hour on demand, and committed pricing is available if you want to reserve capacity. Right now there is no premium for the managed layer. You pay the same rate you'd pay for the bare GPU. That will probably change in the coming months, so it's a good time to get in.

Let's say you keep one 8×H200 worker warm for a month. That's roughly $26,800 on demand, before any commitment discount. The same eight H200s on Together AI's cluster tier are $5.99 per GPU-hour, about $35,000. On Fireworks they're $7.00 per GPU-hour today, about $41,000, and Fireworks has announced an increase to $8.00 on September 1, which takes it to about $47,000.

...

More models, and more modalities: speech-to-text, text-to-speech, text-to-video. A B200 cluster is coming in the next few months and will be available through Managed Endpoints when it lands. And later this year we plan to ship Token Factory, a per-token service on the same infrastructure, so a team that's too small for a dedicated endpoint today can start on the meter and move to a dedicated endpoint when the load justifies it.

results.title: Nvidia GPU Rental Prices Rising Across All Four Generations Simultaneously · The Information Machine
highlights:
Concluded Ran 1 day 4 sources updated 16 Aug 2026

# Nvidia GPU Rental Prices Rising Across All Four Generations Simultaneously

...

Rising prices across multiple GPU generations at once indicate that AI compute demand is broad, not confined to the newest hardware tier. This affects the cost base for organizations renting rather than owning GPU capacity for training and inference.

When stories like this move, I write about them in an email each morning.

The full picture

Rental prices for Nvidia GPUs are rising or holding across four hardware generations simultaneously as of August 2026. The 2020-era A100 is renting at $1.65/hr and rising rather than declining, while H100 neocloud rates sit at $2.74/hr, H200 at $3.28/hr, and B200 at $5.61/hr with high volatility. H100 prices had fallen 64-75% from historical peaks near $8/hr and are stabilizing in a $2.19-$3.50/hr neocloud range depending on provider, while hyperscaler H100 rates remain higher. B200 pricing spiked above $6.00/hr during March 2026 before pulling back. JarvisLabs assessed a 10-20% further H100 decline as possible only if B200 supply expands broadly.

results.title: temperature2 ships /gpu/: what compute actually costs
results.author: The Hardware Desk
highlights:
Published 2026.08.28 · The Hardware Desk 

temperature2's /gpu/ section charts daily GPU rental prices in US dollars per GPU-hour for the H100 SXM, H200, B200, A100 SXM4 and RTX 5090, alongside blended token prices in dollars per million tokens for Anthropic, OpenAI, Google and DeepSeek, both from the Ornn Data public index, plus depreciation, volatility, generational premium and breakeven figures computed from those series.

 TL;DR 

- ▸ An H100 SXM hour settled at $2.68 on 26 August 2026, a B200 hour at $6.22 and an RTX 5090 hour at $0.54 — 92 days of daily settlements, all charted.
- ▸ Token prices fell far harder than rent this month: OpenAI's blended price is down 68.0% over 31 days while H100 rent moved -1.5%.
- ▸ The board carries volatility, rebased depreciation curves, generational ratios and $/PFLOP-hour, all computed here from the published series with the method written next to each number.
- ▸ One GPU-hour has to produce 1.83M tokens to cover its own rent at Anthropic's blended price and 26.15M at DeepSeek's — a 14.28x spread in what a token is worth.
- ▸ Prices are from the Ornn Data public index; the public window is rolling, so the site keeps its own archive and never rewrites a recorded day.

...

The site has a new section. `/gpu/` charts the two prices everything else in AI is denominated in: what an hour of a GPU rents for, and what a million tokens costs. Both are daily series from the Ornn Data public index, both settle a day behind, and both are now on the site with their arithmetic shown. Here is what is on the page, what it says as of the 26 August 2026 settlement, and why a price page is worth building at all.

## The board

Five GPUs, one row each, 92 days of daily settlements from 27 May to 26 August 2026.

| GPU | USD/hour | 92d | Volatility | Range | $/PFLOP-hr |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| B200 | $6.22 | +17.1% | 60% | $4.22 – $7.28 | $2.76 |
| H200 | $4.24 | +8.7% | 97% | $2.99 – $5.62 | $4.29 |
| H100 SXM | $2.68 | -2.9% | 63% | $2.29 – $3.17 | $2.71 |
| A100 SXM4 | $1.06 | -14.5% | 39% | $0.99 – $1.31 | $3.40 |
| RTX 5090 | $0.54 | -37.2% | 74% | $0.48 – $1.33 | $2.58 |

Prices settled 26 August 2026, Ornn Data Compute Price Index. Volatility is the annualized standard deviation of daily log returns scaled by the square root of 365 — calendar days rather than trading days, because compute rents on weekends and a 252-day scaling would understate it by about 17%. That measure, the changes, the ranges and the per-unit columns are all computed on this site from the published daily series, not read from a paid analytics endpoint, which is why the method can be stated instead of cited.

...

`/gpu/#decay` rebases all five series to 100 on 27 May, which is the only honest way to put a $6.22 hour and a $0.54 hour on one axis. Absolute dollars hide the slope, and the slope is the story.

results.author: Aliteq Team
highlights:
On each provider's own pricing page on Nov 3, 2026, Crusoe had the cheapest on-demand H100 ($3.90 a GPU-hour, rising to $4.50 on Dec 1) and Lambda the cheapest B200 ($6.69). CoreWeave was the most expensive on demand, but its fixed spot prices undercut everyone's on-demand rate. The full table, the catches, and where the marketplace tier sits.

...

Which big GPU cloud is cheapest for H100 and B200? On each provider's own pricing page on November 3, 2026: for the H100, Crusoe at $3.90 per GPU-hour on demand, with Lambda a cent behind at $3.99 on an 8-GPU instance. For the B200, Lambda at $6.69 per GPU-hour (8x), well under Nebius ($8.50) and CoreWeave ($8.60). CoreWeave is the most expensive on demand, but if your job can be interrupted its published spot prices ($2.46 an H100, $4.26 a B200, per GPU) undercut everyone's on-demand rate. Two dates to know: Crusoe's own page says its H100 goes to $4.50 on December 1, 2026, which hands the cheapest on-demand H100 to Lambda.

## The short answer (read Nov 3, 2026)

Among CoreWeave, Nebius, Lambda and Crusoe, the cheapest on-demand H100 on November 3, 2026 was Crusoe at $3.90 per GPU-hour, then Lambda at $3.99 (8x instance), Nebius at $4.50 and CoreWeave at $6.16 (an 8-GPU node at $49.24 an hour). Crusoe's page says its H100 rises to $4.50 on December 1, 2026. The cheapest on-demand B200 was Lambda at $6.69 per GPU-hour (8x; $6.99 on one GPU), then Nebius at $8.50 and CoreWeave at $8.60; Crusoe's B200 is contact-sales. For interruptible work, CoreWeave's spot nodes work out to $2.46 per H100 and $4.26 per B200, and Nebius preemptible starts from $0.79 (H100) and $0.99 (B200) at a dynamic rate. Smaller clouds go lower still: Hyperstack listed a B200 at $6.00 and an H100 at $2.50.
